input.quote: 13.6.2 EXCEPT AS OTHERWISE SET FORTH IN THIS ARTICLE 13, NEITHER PARTY MAKES, AND EACH PARTY EXPRESSLY DISCLAIMS, ANY REPRESENTATION OR WARRANTY OF ANY KIND WITH RESPECT TO THE SUBJECT MATTER OF THIS AGREEMENT, EITHER ORAL OR WRITTEN, EXPRESS, IMPLIED, STATUTORY OR OTHERWISE, INCLUDING ANY REPRESENTATION OR WARRANTY REGARDING THE USE, RESULTS OR EFFICACY OF THE PRODUCT.
input.rationale: This is a co-development/funding agreement, not a software or services procurement: PB (our party) is the performing/development party and SFJ is principally the funder, with SFJ acting as sponsor and performing trial activities in the SFJ Territory. Article 13 contains express, largely mutual warranties that cover the elements the playbook cares about on the counterparty side — authority and no conflicting agreements (13.1.1–13.1.2), compliance with law (13.1.3 Anti-Corruption Laws; 13.1.4 debarment certifications; 13.1.5 required certifications, permits and authorisations), and SFJ's funding-capacity warranty (13.5). SFJ's performance standard is set by Section 2.2.2, which requires it to conduct the Clinical Trials and perform all other assigned responsibilities in compliance with the Protocol, all Applicable Laws and the Agreement, and "Applicable Laws" expressly includes GCP/GLP/GMP and ICH guidelines — the industry-standard equivalent of the "professional and workmanlike" standard in this context. Critically, the disclaimer does not swallow the express warranties: 13.6.2 opens "EXCEPT AS OTHERWISE SET FORTH IN THIS ARTICLE 13", so this is not walk-away "AS IS" territory. The 13.6.1 no-warranty on trial outcome/patentability is mutual and, because PB generates the Research Results, operates in our favour, so we do not disturb it. The conformance-period and repair/replace/refund mechanics (12 months / 90 days) have no analogue here as there are no software deliverables; that gap is noted rather than flagged, and remedies for breach run through Article 12 indemnification and Article 14 termination. PB's own warranties are more extensive than SFJ's, but that is the negotiated funding bargain and is addressed under the reps/diligence rules rather than this warranty rule. No redline proposed.
